results.note: Fresh axe-core run (Chromium, 1440x900 and 390x844) on /insights, the debt advisory post, /contact-us and /accessibility-statement reproduces the auditor's numbers: /insights color-contrast serious 26 nodes (card dates and .text-color-grey2 excerpts, #8d8d8d on #ffffff = 3.31:1 at 16px), link-name serious 4 at 1440 and 5 at 390 (.nav_brand-2, mailto, LinkedIn, Instagram icon links, plus .nav_button-2 on mobile), input-button-name critical 1 (footer newsletter <input type=submit value="">), landmark-one-main 1 (zero <main> on every page tested); post: color-contrast 3 (date and 2 footer lines, #8d8d8d on #fffcf5 = 3.23:1, 14px footer). DOM: 6 inputs on pages with the contact form and none has a label[for], wrapping label, aria-label or aria-labelledby; share control is a 28x28 <div class=bi-social-card is-share> with no role or tabindex; BTL post has 6 and hotel post 4 in-article infographics with alt="" (the debt advisory post has none). Statement text verified by curl: 'Designing with sufficient colour contrast', 'Providing meaningful page titles, headings, and link text', 'ensuring form labels are clear', 'WCAG 2.1, Level AA, where reasonably practicable'; the only years on the page are 2000 (FSMA) and the footer 2026, no prepared/reviewed date, no conformance status. One small correction: a generic 'Known limitations' paragraph does exist, it just lists no issues. Lighthouse summary: insights a11y 85, posts 83 and 86. Severity high is fair: a published statement contradicted by measurable defects, including one critical and two serious axe rules.

Independent CDP network capture, cache disabled, full scroll so lazy images load. 1440x900: 57 requests, 12,433 KB encoded, of which images 11,792 KB. Top entries: 6a86c43821b64fd77f76d895_Roscap Blog.png 1,555 KB loaded twice (hero layer and first card thumbnail from the CMS copy 6a8c248c..._Roscap%2520Blog.png), Hotel Financing PNG 1,048 KB, Financing Social Housing-p-1600 1,024 KB, AI Data Centres-p-1600 1,014 KB, Property Portfolio-p-1600 995 KB, BTL PNG 921 KB, roberto unsplash-p-1600 817 KB, Development Exit-p-1600 730 KB, blog4.avif 797 KB, blog2.avif 602 KB, blog3.avif 460 KB. DOM: section.is-header holds two img.hero-bg, both 1440x900, position absolute, z-index -1, opacity 1, display block; the daria-kraplak AVIF (1440x840 natural) is fully covered by the PNG, and the fold screenshot shows only the typewriter PNG. First card img has no srcset and natural 1440x840 at a 582x349 slot; all other PNG cards carry sizes=100vw so the browser picks the -p-1600 (or the original where srcset tops out at 1370w) for a 582 px slot. 390x844: 4,994 KB total after full scroll (Lighthouse's 3,649 KiB was without scrolling), the 1,555 KB no-srcset first card still loads in full while the hero and other cards correctly drop to -p-500 variants. Lighthouse pre-run confirms mobile performance 62 and LCP 6.5 s. Severity high is fair.

Computed styles at 1440x900 on the BTL post, the debt advisory post and /privacy-policy: .w-richtext width 1308 px, max-width none; p 16px/24px Switzer rgb(40,40,40) (legal pages rgb(18,22,29)); h2 40px/40px margin-top 24px; h3 40px/48px, so H2 and H3 are the same size (BTL post has 9 H2 and 20 H3). Measured characters per rendered line with Range.getClientRects: 164 on a full single line (privacy policy), 158 and 130 on 2-line paragraphs whose last line is partial, so 'about 164 per full line' is right. 390x844: p 16px/24px, 41 to 45 characters per line, h2 32px/32px, h3 24px/28.8px (hierarchy is fine on mobile only). H1 64px/83px Boska, 768 px wide, as stated. Screenshot btl-body-1440.png shows body copy running the full container. Lines twice the comfortable maximum on every article and legal page, plus a flat heading hierarchy across 20 sub-sections, clearly hurts readability of the long guides, so high is fair.

All facts reproduce from a fresh curl of the 25 sitemap URLs parsed with an order-independent HTML parser: every one of the 12 posts renders Article JSON-LD with exactly @context, @type, headline, description, url, publisher (no datePublished, dateModified, author, image, mainEntityOfPage); posts have zero og: or twitter: meta tags; the 13 static pages have og:title, og:description, og:type, twitter:card, twitter:title, twitter:description and no og:image anywhere on the site (0 of 25); zero elements, the date is a bare
24 Aug 2026
; canonicals correct on all 25; descriptions 117 to 153 characters. Severity is overstated: Lighthouse SEO is 100 on every page, titles, descriptions and canonicals are correct, the Article markup is valid if thin, and the gaps limit upside (article rich results, share previews with an image) rather than breaking anything. Medium is the fair level; the fix remains cheap.

Re-ran the scan myself over my own curl of the 25 URLs (text extracted with a stdlib parser). Footer disclaimer present on all 25 (25 of 25 files contain 'not authorised or regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority'); 'FCA' as a word 0 hits; every 'authorised' hit is either the footer negation, 'unauthorised' in the policies or 'authorised personnel'; no page states or implies FCA authorisation, which the finding itself says. Every quoted phrase exists: Home 'our team provides advice shaped by current conditions — ensuring every client and project secures the most appropriate form of capital' and 'capital advisory and private investment firm'; BTL 'Higher deposits reduce lender risk and improve mortgage approval chances'; Our Services 'Roscap provides access to: Preferred Equity Fixed-return positions behind senior debt'; hotel post 'attractive returns'; contact FAQ 'as little as 5–10 working days, subject to valuation and legal readiness' and 'typically complete within 6–8 weeks' and 'competitive terms'; partner page 'hundreds of current partners', 'commissions in perpetuity', 'recurring revenue stream with minimal work'; Privacy, Terms and Disclaimer all contain 'renovation finance, buy-to-let mortgages, and commercial mortgages'; Track Record '12% IRR' and '14% IRR'. Corrections: the '5 phrases that should change' are 4 term hits on 2 sentences (the auditor's own table has 4 CHANGE rows: advice and secure on the Home sentence, approved and mortgage on the BTL sentence). Of those two, the Home 'ensuring every client ... secures' outcome promise is a fair change; 'advice' itself matches the Disclaimer's own 'provides advice only in relation to unregulated activities'. The BTL line is a generic statement about how lenders assess deposits in an educational article, not a promise about Roscap's service, so it belongs in 'review' rather than 'change'. With no FCA-implying copy found and the live items being soft outcome language and caveated timescales, this is a review list, not a compliance breach: medium, not high.

Reproduced: curl of all 25 URLs finds <script src="https://jj59l3.csb.app/script.js"> on exactly /insights and /about-us, in <body>, with no integrity or crossorigin attribute. Fetched the script: 1,486 bytes, HTTP 200 via Cloudflare with cache-control 'private, max-age=0, no-cache, no-store' (fetched on every page view), content is a GSAP ScrollTrigger counter for .stats-cards-wrap/.stats-num-span and a Swiper init for '.slider-wrap .swiper'. Playwright runtime at 1440 confirms the request fires on both pages (200). Detail correction: neither page has the elements it targets. /insights and /about-us both contain 0 .stats-cards-wrap and 0 .slider-wrap (grep of the HTML class attributes and runtime querySelectorAll), so the script is dead code on both, not just on Insights; the only page with those elements is the Home page (1 each, counters 19/38/7 animate there) and it does not load the csb.app script. So the recommendation 'paste the script into About only' is wrong: delete the tag from both pages, and delete Swiper from Insights (Swiper 12 loads there with no .swiper element; About does have swiper-initialized 0 too). Severity stays high: an ephemeral, editable third-party sandbox host executing JavaScript without SRI on two live pages that carry the contact form is a supply-chain risk regardless of the code being useless, and removal is free.

Fresh Playwright runs at 1440x900, 1024x768 and 390x844 on /partner-program, never clicking. The page-bottom form #wf-form-Contact-Form (name, email, Phone, Subject, Message) has one <input type=submit class='button golden formbuttonhide-desktop w-button' fs-mirrorclick-element=target>; the site CSS roscap-site.webflow.shared.e12c5bf0f.css sets .button.golden.formbuttonhide-desktop {display:none} outside any media query and display:block only inside @media (max-width: 991px). Measured: at 1440 and 1024 the real submit is display none, 0x0, offsetParent null; the visible gold 'Submit' is <a href='#' fs-mirrorclick-element='trigger' class='button golden w-button'> at 84x41. CDP DOMDebugger.getEventListeners on that anchor returns an empty list at all three viewports, it has no onclick and no jQuery handlers, and the form itself has no direct listeners. No Finsweet script is present: script hosts are googletagmanager, cloudfront (jQuery), website-files (Webflow chunks, GSAP) and jsdelivr (Swiper only); window.FinsweetAttributes and window.fsAttributes are undefined. At 390 the real button is shown (84x41) and the anchor collapses to 0x0, so mobile works. /blogs/development-exit-finance has the identical pattern and also loads no Finsweet script, while /, /contact-us, /about-us and /insights load cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@finsweet/attributes@2/attributes.js (FinsweetAttributes is an object there). Also noted: the brochure lead-gen form on the same page uses the same mirror-click target attribute. One nuance not in the finding: implicit submission by pressing Enter in a text field would still reach the hidden default button, so keyboard users might submit; this was not tested because it would submit a live form. For mouse and touch users on desktop and tablet the only visible Submit does nothing, so critical is fair.

Fresh browser context per page and viewport (1440 and 390), en-GB locale, no interaction, 2.5 s after networkidle, on /partner-program, /contact-us, /contact-us-success, a 404 URL and /. On every load: <head> contains <script async src='https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js?id=G-H8HS2R6NLS'> plus the inline gtag config, dataLayer is ['js', date], ['config','G-H8HS2R6NLS'] with no consent default call (no script on any page contains 'consent'); requests go to analytics.google.com/g/collect (en=page_view) and stats.g.doubleclick.net/g/collect with gcd=13l3l3l3l1l1, npa=0, no gcs parameter, which is the signature of no Consent Mode defaults. Cookies after first paint on every page: _ga and _ga_H8HS2R6NLS on .roscap.co.uk, 400 days, plus _cfuvid (Cloudflare, session, httpOnly). /contact-us-success additionally sets _gcl_au (90 days), localStorage key _gcl_ls, fires three analytics hits with en=generate_lead and three requests to www.google.com/measurement/conversion, all on a plain page load. DOM search for cookie or consent elements found nothing except the footer 'Cookie Policy' link; localStorage is otherwise empty; screenshots show no banner. The Cookie Policy text (curl) says 'Non-essential cookies are used only where you have provided consent via our cookie banner', 'Our cookie banner/preference centre provides the current cookie list' and 'using the cookie preference link in the website footer (if enabled)'; the Privacy Policy says 'subject to your cookie preferences' and 'consent where cookies are not strictly necessary'. Analytics and advertising cookies set and hits sent without consent under PECR, while the policies describe controls that do not exist: critical is fair.

Most measurements reproduce at 1440x900: section.is-header 900 px (min-height 900px), H1 64px, hero paragraph 57 words / 380 characters at 18px white, 772 px wide, 7 lines, over partner hero bg webp with .hero-bg-overlay.is-green rgba(4,52,53,0.6), no link or button inside the hero; .pr-cards-grid min-height 394px, four .pr-cards 312x394 with justify-content space-between, icon 83 px, text 72 to 108 px; 'How Our Partner Program Works' is a Swiper (.join-swiper) with 6 text-only slides, 3 fully visible, steps 04 to 06 off-screen until Next is used, slide text matches the quoted steps including 'receive commissions in perpetuity'; below the hero the only images are 4 line icons, arrow SVGs, 8 unlabelled partner logos and two decorative background SVGs, no photograph, person or number; the closing form is the same 5-field form under the Home headline 'Let's discuss your next transaction, funding requirement, or investment opportunity.' At 390: hero 844 px, paragraph 14px, 10 lines. Three details are wrong or missing: (1) on mobile each .pr-cards is 358x236, not 'about 400 px tall'; (2) the carousel cards are 432x432 squares with computed aspect-ratio auto, not 4/5 (the title is still pushed to the bottom with the upper half empty, as the screenshot shows); (3) the page already has a gold 'Join The Program' button directly under the four cards, but it links to /contact-us rather than the page's own form, which the evidence does not mention and the recommendation should account for. The owner has already named this page as dry, so the diagnosis stands; high is acceptable with the corrected details.

Live page (curl and Playwright): hero paragraph 'Join hundreds of current partners who are successfully working with Roscap to support their client's capital requirements.' (1 hit) and carousel step 06 'As Roscap completes subsequent deals with the client, receive commissions in perpetuity' (1 hit); the Our Partners grid shows 8 logos with no names. Brochure: the page has no PDF link, the file URL is the lead-gen form's data-redirect; I downloaded it independently (HTTP 200, 9,211,904 bytes, 5 pages, image-only with a damaged xref, read via pypdf image extraction and viewed). Page 4 'TERMS & CONDITIONS' reads 'The Partner works exclusively with Roscap', 'The Partner will receive a 25% introductory referral fee for the first deal completed. For all future transactions with the same Client, the Partner will receive a 10% referral fee in perpetuity.', 'All referral fees are paid from the total deal commissions that Roscap receives.'; page 4 also repeats 'Join hundreds of current partners'. Page 2 reads 'Roscap has established over 1000 relationships with capital partners across the globe' and additionally 'putting together the best capital structure for your deal'. The context brief confirms both headline claims are unconfirmed with the owner. Unverified volume claims on the live page plus perpetual fee promises and an exclusivity obligation stated only in marketing material: high is fair.

Live page: card 2 reads 'Earn an additional recurring revenue stream with minimal work' (confirmed by text scan and screenshot). Brochure (independently downloaded from the form's data-redirect URL and viewed page by page): page 2 'Roscap is a real estate private equity and debt firm.'; page 3 'Debt Capital Raising' lists 'Facility Types: Bridging, Development Finance, Investment Loans, Mezzanine Finance', 'Loan Amount: £100,000 to £100,000,000', 'Interest Rate: Starting from 4% p.a.', 'Loan-to-Value Ratio: Up to 90%', 'Timelines: 6-36 months'. Footer on all 25 URLs: 'undertakes introductory activities and provides advisory services solely in relation to unregulated activities' and 'not authorised or regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority'. Privacy Policy, Disclaimer and Terms each list 'buy-to-let mortgages' among the finance types. All quoted wording is accurate. The on-site exposure is one line of puffery; the weight sits in the gated brochure, where a self-description as a 'private equity and debt firm' and a headline rate and LTV conflict with the site's stated positioning as an unregulated introducer and advisory firm and fall squarely under the owner's rule to flag rate promises. High is fair, framed for compliance review as the finding does.
